newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - new deals, CPI ahead.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - new deals, CPI ahead.

text.p: The U.S. municipal bond market was officially closed Monday in observance of Columbus Day, but the week ahead holds some key economic data and roughly $2.446 billion of new issues.

On Wednesday, the market is scheduled to receive September Consumer Price Index data. Economists polled by Reuters expect a 0.3 percent increase, both overall and in the core rate, which excludes the more volatile food and energy prices.
Thursday will bring September data on industrial production and capacity utilization as well as housing starts and jobless claims for the week ended Oct. 12.
Also Thursday, the market is scheduled to receive the October Philadelphia Federal Reserve Banks business survey.
As for new deals, the week's negotiated issues are expected to total $1.349 billion in 42 offerings, while competitive deals are expected to total $1.097 billion in 63 offerings.

The largest negotiated issue is a $375 million New York City Municipal Finance Water Authority bond offering through PaineWebber Inc. San Francisco International Airport will bring the largest competitive deal, a $275 million two-part issue at 1100 EDT on Tuesday.
